system_type_reason: Terminal-first personal AI agent used directly by end users.

repo_overview.summary: gptme is a terminal-first personal AI agent. The LLM emits tool calls as markdown codeblocks or native tool-calls (shell, python, patch, browser, ...), which run in the local environment and whose output is fed back into the conversation. Around the core loop sit an extensive hook system, context compression, lessons injection, subagents, an HTTP/ACP server and an eval harness.

components.purpose: core loop: _run_chat_loop / _process_message_conversation / step(), message model, codeblock parsing
cross-cutting single modules: circuit breaker for tool/MCP calls, checkpoints/snapshots, prompt queue
provider backends (Anthropic, OpenAI, Responses API, plugins), model metadata/resolution, validation
tool implementations: shell, python, patch/save/read, browser, subagent/, autocompact/, todo, complete, mcp adapter, precommit, ...
hook registry and built-in hooks: confirmation, cost/token/time/cache awareness, injection screening, markdown validation, auto snapshots
conversation persistence, event log, conversation checkpoints
lessons/skills system: matching and auto-inclusion of guidance into context
helpers: cost tracking, token counting, context dedup/reduce, output storage, interrupt handling, ask_execute
entry points: CLI, persistent autonomous agents (service), Agent Client Protocol, Flask HTTP API/web UI
benchmark harness (SWE-bench, tbench, suites), pass-rate gate

topology.justification: The default system is one agent: a single chat() loop with one model and one system prompt calling tools via step()/reply() (chat.py:554-562). The opt-in subagent tool (disabled_by_default, subagent/__init__.py:384) adds an orchestrator-worker structure: each subagent runs its own chat() loop with its own model, profile/system prompt and tool set in a thread, subprocess or ACP process (subagent/execution.py:321-331), and its result returns to the parent via the LOOP_CONTINUE completion hook. These subagents are full agents, so with the tool enabled the system is multi-agent.

resilience.name: MCP call protection: reconnect-retry and per-server circuit breaker
resilience.what_it_is: Two layers around MCP tool calls. On a connection error the MCP client is restarted and the call retried once. Around the call sits a CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN circuit breaker, one instance per MCP server: after 5 consecutive failures the breaker opens and every call fails fast with CircuitOpenError(retry_after) for a 30 s cooldown; afterwards a single probe call is let through, which either resets to CLOSED or restarts the cooldown. User cancellations (MCPInterruptedError) are excluded from failure counting.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps MCPClient.call_tool, i.e. the execution of an MCP tool inside a step. Contains a failing or hanging MCP server so that repeated tool calls return immediately with an error the agent can see. Otherwise every call to a broken server would block on the transport again and burn time and turns.

resilience.name: hard step limit per turn
resilience.what_it_is: GPTME_MAX_STEPS env variable caps the number of step() iterations inside one user turn; on reaching it the loop breaks and appends a system message 'Stopped: reached max steps limit'.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the end of each iteration of the inner tool loop in _process_message_conversation. Bounds runaway tool loops and the cost and time they consume. Otherwise a model that keeps emitting tool calls runs indefinitely.

resilience.name: user interrupt and decline with feedback to the model
resilience.what_it_is: Ctrl-C during generation or during a tool run aborts the current step, appends the system message 'Interrupted by user' (with the tool's call_id when inside a tool) and clears the prompt queue. A declined tool confirmation ('Execution declined by user') likewise ends the tool loop and returns to the user prompt. The interactive system prompt instructs the model to ask the user for clarification after an abort.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the outer loop, in the inner tool loop and in execute_msg. Lets the human stop a wrong or runaway action at any point while the session survives, and records the interruption in the log so the next model turn knows the action did not complete. Otherwise an interrupt kills the session or the model assumes the aborted action succeeded.

def _cwd_session_id(cwd: str) -> str:
    """Derive a deterministic session ID from a workspace path.

    Returns a stable ID like ``acp-<hash8>`` so that the same CWD always
    maps to the same session, enabling session resume across editor restarts.
    """
    h = hashlib.sha256(str(Path(cwd).resolve()).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"acp-{h}"

# --- Session resume: derive a deterministic ID from CWD ---
# This ensures the same workspace always maps to the same session,
# so editor restarts resume the previous conversation.
if cwd:
    session_id = _cwd_session_id(cwd)
    logdir = logs_dir / session_id
    logfile = logdir / "conversation.jsonl"

    if existing and existing.log is not None:

resilience.name: fault-tolerant codeblock tool-call parsing
resilience.what_it_is: Context-aware markdown fence parser that repairs known model formatting errors: concatenated fences ('``````shell'), a closing fence glued to '<think>', nested blocks, and half-closed blocks while streaming. Codeblocks inside thinking sections, including unclosed ones, are skipped.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model response and execute_msg: ToolUse.iter_from_content relies on it to find runnable tool calls. Recovers tool calls from malformed output of specific models (comments name Claude and Gemini). Otherwise such tool calls are lost, split wrongly, or code from the model's thinking gets executed.

# Recover from malformed adjacent outer fences where a block closes and the
# next one opens on the same line, e.g. "``````patch file.py" instead of
# "```\n```patch file.py". ToolUse._to_markdown always emits triple fences,
# so six leading backticks followed immediately by a language tag is a good
# signal that the first three backticks belong to the previous block.
if re.match(r"^`{6}[^`\s]", line):
    line = line[3:]
    lines[i] = line

# Some models concatenate the closing fence with a thinking tag,
# e.g. "```<think>". Recover by treating the leading fence as the
# closing delimiter and reprocessing the remainder on the same line.

    yield Codeblock(
        lang,
        "\n".join(content_lines),
        start=start_line,
        fence="`" * fence_len,

resilience.name: LLM API retry with exponential backoff for transient errors
resilience.what_it_is: Provider decorators retry_on_overloaded (Anthropic) and retry_on_openai_error (all OpenAI-compatible providers) retry up to 5 times with delay 1s * 2^attempt. Only transient errors are retried: 5xx, 429, connection and httpx protocol errors, and messages containing 'overload'/'internal'/'timeout'; everything else (402, auth) is re-raised immediately. Generator variants for streaming retry only while no chunk has been yielded yet. Underneath, the Anthropic SDK client adds its own max_retries=5 and a configurable LLM_API_TIMEOUT.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the provider chat/stream functions called by reply() inside every step(). Absorbs rate limits, provider overloads and dropped connections before they reach the agent loop, and avoids duplicated output by refusing to retry a stream that already emitted content. Otherwise a single transient provider error aborts the step and the session.

resilience.name: prompt caching with targeted cache breakpoints
resilience.what_it_is: apply_cache_control places Anthropic cache_control 'ephemeral' markers on the system prompt, on the last two user messages, and on the last stable message before the first ephemeral (TTL) message. Applied for the native Anthropic API and for Anthropic models via OpenRouter. The system prompt is ordered static first, with an explicit SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY message before the session-volatile context_cmd and chat-history sections, and the time section carries only the date to keep the prefix stable.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs during message preparation for every LLM call. Keeps the stable conversation prefix cached across steps, including when ephemeral context messages expire, which cuts input-token cost and latency of each step. Otherwise every step re-bills the full growing context at the uncached rate.

resilience.name: stream cut-off at first complete tool call
resilience.what_it_is: While streaming, the response is checked at cheap breakpoints (newline, '}' or '>' depending on tool format) for a complete runnable tool use; when one is found, generation stops and the remaining stream is drained only for usage metadata. Default is on for models without parallel tool-call support, overridable via GPTME_BREAK_ON_TOOLUSE.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside _reply_stream, between generation and tool execution. Pauses inference after the first finished tool call so the tool runs before the model continues, which keeps the model from writing on top of unexecuted actions or invented tool output and saves the output tokens of the discarded continuation. Otherwise the model keeps generating past its own tool call.

resilience.name: human confirmation gate for tool execution
resilience.what_it_is: Before a tool runs, get_confirmation queries the registered TOOL_CONFIRM hooks in priority order. The CLI hook shows a preview/diff and asks [Y/n/c/e/a]: the user can decline, edit the content before execution, or auto-confirm the next N calls; the server hook blocks on an SSE/HTTP round-trip to the client. An exception inside a confirmation hook results in skipping the call. A skip is returned to the log as a system message; edits are announced with '(content was edited by user)'. A higher-priority allowlist hook auto-confirms read-only shell pipelines (ls, cat, grep, ... without redirections or find -exec), so the human is asked only for risky commands. In the ACP adapter a permission request that times out after 60 s or fails is treated as a denial.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the model's tool call and its execution (ask_execute / ToolUse.execute) in every step. Lets a human stop or correct a harmful or wrong action before it touches the environment, and fails safe when the confirmation path itself breaks. Otherwise every model-generated shell command, patch or file write runs unreviewed.

resilience.name: prompt-injection screening of untrusted tool output
resilience.what_it_is: TOOL_EXECUTE_POST hook that checks output of tools fetching external content (browser, gh, elicit, URL reads) against 11 regex injection patterns ('ignore previous instructions', '<|im_start|>system', 'your new task is', ...). On a match it appends a system message '[UNTRUSTED: possible prompt injection detected in <tool> output, matching pattern: ...]' right after the tool output.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits after tool execution, before the next generation. Marks injected instructions from web pages or GitHub content as untrusted data for the model. Otherwise the agent may follow instructions planted in fetched content. Detection is deterministic; the protective effect depends on the model heeding the warning.

resilience.name: truncated codeblock detection with model feedback

resilience.name: token budget awareness for the model

Otherwise the model has no signal about remaining context until the window is exhausted. How it reacts is up to the model.

resilience.name: session cost warnings in the model context

# How often the health monitor runs (seconds)
_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 30
# Max idle time before a session is cleaned up (minutes)
_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MINUTES = 60

def _run_health_check() -> None:
    """Single health check iteration."""
    # 1. Clean inactive sessions (was never called before this change).
    # Note: this intentionally applies to all sessions (not just ACP ones) —
    # the health monitor acts as server-wide session hygiene in ACP deployments.
    # Non-ACP sessions idle for more than _SESSION_MAX_AGE_MINUTES are also evicted.
    SessionManager.clean_inactive_sessions(max_age_minutes=_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MINUTES)

    # 2. Check ACP subprocess health
    for session_id, session in SessionManager.get_all_sessions():
        # Snapshot to a local variable: a concurrent _cleanup_all_acp_sessions()
        # can set session.acp_runtime = None between reads, causing AttributeError.
        acp_runtime = session.acp_runtime
        if acp_runtime is None:
            continue
        if session.generating:
            continue  # Don't disturb active generation
        if not acp_runtime.is_subprocess_alive():
            # Re-check generating flag before removing to narrow the TOCTOU window:
            # a /step request arriving between the check above and remove_session()
            # could start a generation on a session we are about to delete.
            if session.generating:
                continue
            logger.warning(
                "ACP subprocess dead for session %s (conversation=%s, pid=%s), "
                "cleaning up",
                session_id,
                session.conversation_id,
                acp_runtime.process_pid,
            )
            # Null out acp_runtime before remove_session so it doesn't
            # spawn a close_acp_runtime_bg thread for an already-dead process.
            session.acp_runtime = None
            SessionManager.remove_session(session_id)

_STUCK_GENERATING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES = 10

@classmethod
def clean_inactive_sessions(cls, max_age_minutes: int = 60) -> None:
    """Clean up inactive sessions.

    Also detects sessions stuck in generating=True state: if a session has
    been generating for longer than _STUCK_GENERATING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES, it is
    force-cleaned to prevent permanent resource leaks.

    Removal is performed atomically under a single lock acquisition to
    prevent a TOCTOU race where a concurrent ``/step`` could start
    generating on a session between the staleness check and its removal.
    Side-effects (hook triggers, ACP cleanup) run after the lock is
    released.
    """
    now = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)
    cutoff = now - timedelta(minutes=max_age_minutes)
    stuck_cutoff = now - timedelta(minutes=cls._STUCK_GENERATING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES)

    # Collect post-lock work: (conversation_id, is_last, acp_runtime)
    deferred: list[tuple[str, bool, AcpSessionRuntime | None]] = []

    with cls._lock:
        to_remove: list[str] = []
        for session_id, session in cls._sessions.items():
            if session.last_activity < cutoff and not session.generating:
                to_remove.append(session_id)
            elif (
                session.generating
                and session.generating_since is not None
                and session.generating_since < stuck_cutoff
            ):
                logger.warning(
                    "Force-cleaning stuck session %s (generating since %s, "
                    "exceeded %d min timeout)",
                    session_id,
                    session.generating_since.isoformat(),
                    cls._STUCK_GENERATING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES,
                )
                session.generating = False
                to_remove.append(session_id)
